subtype: Approach: leading the caregiver by hand [Revision]
passage:
"Tedi! Tedi!" Zeynep cried from the living room. Dalia, Zeynep's mother, was drying dishes. "One minute, Zeynep!"
The calling stopped. Zeynep marched into the kitchen, seized Dalia's finger and pulled toward the sofa, the other hand jabbing at the gap. "Oh, teddy fell behind?" Dalia knelt down, reached in and fished it out. Zeynep hugged it, then patted Dalia's cheek.

qa.q: What did Zeynep grab to pull Dalia to the sofa?
qa.a: Zeynep seized Dalia's finger and pulled toward the sofa.

qa.q: What was Zeynep feeling when Dalia said "One minute"?
qa.a: Zeynep was impatient and worried about the teddy, but stayed determined and found another way to make Dalia understand.

qa.q: What other approach could Zeynep use next time, and why?
qa.a: Zeynep could point and say "stuck" while walking over, because words plus pointing might help Dalia understand even faster.

qa.q: How does Dalia see the finger-pulling?
qa.a: Dalia was busy and did not know what was wrong, but the pull and the pointing showed her clearly, so she came and fixed it.

grounding: When mother says "wait a minute," a toddler grabs her finger and leads her to the sofa, pointing at the teddy, which fixes the missing message.

subtype: Approach: leading the caregiver by hand [Revision]
passage: My name is Gopika, and I was visiting Omkar's mother on Saturday. His ball had rolled under the sofa. "Aai, ball!" he said. She was chopping and said, "Wait a minute." Omkar stood still for a second. Then he grabbed her finger and pulled, hard, all the way to the sofa, and pointed under it. She laughed and knelt. I thought, he's worked out that talking wasn't enough.

qa.q: What did Omkar's mother say when he first asked?
What was Gopika thinking as she watched Omkar pull his mother?
qa.a: Gopika felt impressed and amused, sensing Omkar had worked out that talking wasn't enough.

qa.q: What else could Omkar's mother do next time?
qa.a: She could look where he points straight away, so he doesn't need to drag her.

qa.q: What might pulling his mother to the sofa be like for Omkar?
qa.a: It probably feels satisfying: after "wait a minute" left him stuck, leading her by the finger gets his ball back quickly.

grounding: An observer watches a toddler pull his mother by the finger to the sofa after she says "wait a minute," bringing her to the problem.

subtype: Approach: leading the caregiver by hand [Revision]
passage:
Monday: Baljeet's teddy went under the divan. "Mama!" he called. Kalyani said, "Wait a minute," and forgot.
Wednesday: the teddy went under again. "Mama!" "Wait a minute." Baljeet waited, then trotted over, gripped her finger and tugged her to the divan, pointing.
Friday: before calling at all, Baljeet took her finger and led her there.

qa.q: What did Baljeet do on Friday?
qa.a: Before calling at all, he took her finger and led her there.

qa.q: What was Baljeet feeling when Kalyani forgot on Monday?
qa.a: He was probably disappointed and frustrated that his teddy stayed under the divan.

qa.q: What would you change first if you were Kalyani?
qa.a: Come and look when he first calls, so he knows asking works and needn't tug.

qa.q: How does Baljeet's new plan look to Kalyani?
qa.a: She finds she can't miss the message any more, which may make her realise how often she said wait.

grounding: Over several days a toddler learns to lead his mother by the finger to the problem after "wait a minute" leaves him unheard.
